segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: The dinner in Spanish is la cena,

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: spelled C-E-N-A, la cena.

segments.speaker: Student
segments.text: La cena.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: La cena. Those in Spain will pronounce la cena.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: So la cena, the dinner.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: Now to dine, which doesn't sound formal in Spanish as it does in English,

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: to dine, you just make la cena into a verb.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: So how do you think that would sound?

segments.speaker: Student
segments.text: Cenar.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: Cenar, good. So cenar is to dine.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: So how would you say I was dining or, more naturally in English, I was having dinner?

segments.speaker: Student
segments.text: Cenaba.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: Good, cenaba. Now, apart from I was having dinner, what else could that mean, cenaba?

segments.speaker: Student
segments.text: He, she, it were having dinner.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: And who else?

segments.speaker: Student
segments.text: You formal.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: Good. So we have all of those meanings there with the -aba.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: So for this line in the past, we have -aba for -ar verbs. We are taking off our -ar and we're putting -aba as our key sound, and then we are adding on -mos or -n or -s.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: Quemar, Q-U-E-M-A-R, quemar, in Spanish is to burn.

segments.speaker: Student
segments.text: Quemar.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: Quemar, good.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: How would you say he was burning the dinner? He was burning the dinner.

segments.speaker: Student
segments.text: Quemaba la cena.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: Good, quemaba la cena. And if you wanted to show that it was he that was burning the dinner, how would you do that?

segments.speaker: Student
segments.text: Just él. Él quemaba la cena.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: Good. And if you wanted to show that it was you, formal, you were burning the dinner?

segments.speaker: Student
segments.text: Usted quemaba la cena.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: Good, usted quemaba la cena. Good.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: So, él quemaba la cena. He was burning, and then we say what he was burning, the dinner.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: If we want to say the dinner was burning, the dinner was getting burned, we can't just say la cena quemaba because we're waiting to hear what was the dinner burning. It feels incomplete.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: So if you want to just say the dinner was burning, like the dinner was getting burned, in Spanish we are going to say the dinner was burning itself. What is itself?

segments.speaker: Student
segments.text: Se.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: Se. So how would you say the dinner was burning, the dinner was getting burned, the dinner was burning itself?

segments.speaker: Student
segments.text: La cena se quemaba.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: Very good, yeah. That's it! La cena se quemaba, good.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: The position of la cena is also flexible. You can say la cena se quemaba or you can put la cena afterwards. How would that be?

segments.speaker: Student
segments.text: Se quemaba la cena.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: Se quemaba la cena. So it's flexible, unlike in English, because in English, well, we don't really change verbs so much. There are not so many grammatical resources in English as there are in Spanish, for example. So in English, the word order is much more important than in Spanish to show what's going on. So we can say la cena se quemaba or se quemaba la cena.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: Because we have se, we understand that the dinner was getting burned. There was nobody else there involved.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: If you want to say I burn, like in the sun, in the sense of, you know, I get burnt, you're also going to use this structure, no? You're going to say I burn myself in the sun. Now you understand you're not burning yourself, it just means I get burnt. So sun is sol. In was?

segments.speaker: Student
segments.text: En.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: En. So, I get burnt, I burn, in the sun. How would that be? And sun is masculine.

segments.speaker: Student
segments.text: Me quemo en el sol.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: Good, me quemo en el sol. You can't just say quemo en el sol because this would mean that I burn something in the sun and we all be waiting to hear what you burn in the sun. Me quemo en el sol.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: If you want to say the sun burns me, this is another way you could put the sentence and there we are not using this self structure because we have the sun burns and then we have me telling us what it burns, so it's complete. So how would you say that, the sun burns me?

segments.speaker: Student
segments.text: El sol me quema.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: Good. El sol me quema, me quema el sol, either way.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: Another example of a verb like this is romper. Romper. Romper means, maybe you can guess it. What do you think romper means? It's it's quite obscure, the connection, but you might find it. Rupture?

segments.speaker: Student
segments.text: To break.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: To break. Romper, to break. So how would you say I break?

segments.speaker: Student
segments.text: Rompo.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: Rompo, with a P, rompo. I break it?

segments.speaker: Student
segments.text: Lo rompo.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: Lo rompo, good, I break it. If you want to say it breaks, like it gets broken, it breaks all the time. All the time is todo el tiempo. Literally, all, todo, el tiempo, the time. Todo, T-O-D-O, is all. So it breaks all the time, it breaks itself, it gets broken all the time. How would you say that, it breaks all the time?

segments.speaker: Student
segments.text: Se rompa todo...

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: The se got your attention, so you forgot to do something very important which was to quickly go back to the to-form and and be clear on what type of verb you're working with.

segments.speaker: Student
segments.text: Se rompe todo el tiempo.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: Good. Se rompe todo el tiempo. It breaks all the time. So here we understand that it gets broken, it breaks, it breaks itself. How would you say they break all the time?

segments.speaker: Student
segments.text: It's rompen... and se rompen todo el tiempo.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: Se rompen todo el tiempo. They break themselves, not literally that they are breaking themselves, just they get broken. We don't have this get in Spanish, and this is how we get around it. What was tonight?

segments.speaker: Student
segments.text: Esta noche.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: Esta noche. So we said esta is this for feminine words, esta noche. What was this for masculine words? How did we say this car?

segments.speaker: Student
segments.text: Este auto.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: Este auto, este coche, good. So este is this for masculine words, and we have the E of él, like el auto, in este, este auto.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: These cars are estos autos.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: So we go from este to estos for the plural, not estes, huh? Estos, estos autos.

segments.speaker: Student
segments.text: Estos autos.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: Now, this might look irregular, but there is a logic there. It's just different to the one that we might expect. We have the E of él in este, and we have the -os of los in estos. So, we have the car?

segments.speaker: Student
segments.text: El coche.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: Good. And this car?

segments.speaker: Student
segments.text: Este coche.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: Good. The cars?

segments.speaker: Student
segments.text: Los coches.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: Los coches. And these cars?

segments.speaker: Student
segments.text: Estos coches.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: Estos coches. So we have -os in los and estos, and we have E in él and este.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: All of those you can make that and those now, just by plucking out the T. So if este auto is this car, how do you say that car?

segments.speaker: Student
segments.text: Ese auto.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: Ese auto. If estos coches or estos autos are these cars, how would you say those cars?

segments.speaker: Student
segments.text: Esos autos.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: Esos autos, good. So how would you say those ones, and for those ones you can just use this word for those, and imagine we're talking about masculine things or mixed things, things of mixed gender. Those ones break all the time. Those ones break all the time.

segments.speaker: Student
segments.text: Esos rompen todo el tiempo.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: So now I'm waiting to hear what they break. Esos rompen todo el tiempo... What what do they break all the time?

segments.speaker: Student
segments.text: Esos se rompen todo el tiempo.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: Good! Esos se rompen todo el tiempo. So you'll have to listen out in Spanish for these verbs that want you to show it when the action isn't to something else. It's transforming, not something else, se transforma. It breaks, it's breaking, not something else, se rompe. It's changing, not something else, but here you don't need it: cambia, from cambiar, cambia.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: Being aware of that this occurs is enough and we will listen out and in real life get that conscious understanding and also an intuition about where we need to do this.
